matchstick.title: Move vertical I-stick between numerals
matchstick.principle: Detach a single vertical stick that forms an I from one numeral and attach it to another numeral that can accept a vertical stick, ensuring both source and destination remain valid Roman numerals.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation can be balanced by transferring value between numerals, especially when an I can be moved without breaking the source numeral.
matchstick.example: Removing a vertical stick from an I and leaving the original numeral missing, resulting in an invalid symbol.

matchstick.title: Prefer intra-character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: First explore moving a stick within the same character (e.g., turning X into V or I into L) before considering moves that affect other characters.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of the search, check if a single stick can be repositioned inside a numeral to form another valid numeral.
matchstick.example: Skipping a possible X→V transformation and directly moving a stick to another character.

matchstick.title: Validate symbols after stick move
matchstick.principle: After detaching a stick, verify that both the originating symbol and the destination symbol still correspond to valid Roman numeral characters or operators.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after any stick relocation, before evaluating the arithmetic.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal from X, leaving X as a single diagonal which is not a valid symbol.

matchstick.title: Avoid single angled sticks
matchstick.principle: A lone diagonal stick does not constitute a valid Roman numeral; V and X must consist of two diagonals, so never leave a single diagonal after a move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a diagonal is removed from V or X, ensure the source still has two diagonals or is replaced by another valid shape.
matchstick.example: Removing one diagonal from V and leaving a single diagonal stick.

matchstick.title: Convert plus to minus by removing vertical stick
matchstick.principle: A plus sign consists of a vertical and a horizontal stick; removing the vertical stick turns it into a minus sign.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a plus sign appears and a vertical stick can be repurposed elsewhere to adjust numeral values.
matchstick.example: Leaving a plus sign unchanged while a vertical stick could be removed to make a minus sign.

matchstick.title: Create new numeral by reordering stick
matchstick.principle: A detached stick can be placed as a separate character, forming a new numeral (e.g., adding a vertical stick to create an I).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When an extra stick is available after a move and a new numeral could help balance the equation.
matchstick.example: Leaving a detached vertical stick unused instead of forming a new I.

matchstick.title: Consider inter-character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If no intra‑character move yields a valid equality, explore moving a stick from one character to another character (including operators) while preserving validity.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After exhausting intra‑character possibilities without success.
matchstick.example: Only trying intra‑character moves and missing a solution that requires moving a stick from one numeral to another.

matchstick.title: Swap operators via horizontal stick move
matchstick.principle: The equals sign (=) consists of two horizontal sticks; moving one of them to a minus sign (-) turns the minus into an equals and the equals into a minus.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains both = and - (or +) and a horizontal stick can be transferred without breaking the symbols.
matchstick.example: Swapping = and - but failing to verify whether the resulting arithmetic holds.

matchstick.title: Augment numeral with vertical stick from operator
matchstick.principle: When converting a plus sign to a minus sign by removing its vertical stick, the removed stick can be attached to a numeral to increase its value.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a plus sign is present and a numeral could benefit from an extra vertical stick (e.g., turning I into II).
matchstick.example: Ignoring the opportunity to add a detached vertical stick to a numeral after turning + into -.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic after stick move
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick and forming new Roman numerals and operators, compute the numeric values of each side to ensure the equality truly holds.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After any candidate transformation, before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.example: Swapping operators and assuming the equation is solved without checking the numeric result.

matchstick.description: Overlooking intra‑character transformations (e.g., X→V) before inter‑character moves
matchstick.why_it_happens: The solver focuses on moving sticks between characters and forgets that many puzzles can be solved by reshaping a single numeral.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: First enumerate all intra‑character stick relocations (e.g., X→V, I↔L) and test them before considering inter‑character moves.

matchstick.description: Assuming sticks retain their orientation and not rotating horizontals to verticals (or vice versa) when repositioning
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model conflates stick length with orientation, assuming any stick can be placed in any direction.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Keep the original orientation of each stick; a horizontal remains horizontal, a vertical remains vertical, and a diagonal remains diagonal when relocated.

matchstick.description: Not evaluating the arithmetic result after each candidate transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The solver assumes that fixing the symbols automatically fixes the equality.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After any stick move, compute the numeric values of both sides and confirm the equality before finalizing.

matchstick.description: Assuming operator swaps (e.g., = ↔ -) automatically solve the puzzle
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sees a syntactic change and expects the arithmetic to align without verification.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Treat operator swaps as a candidate move; always follow with an arithmetic check.

matchstick.description: Ignoring the I↔L transformation (adding/removing a horizontal stick to/from an I)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The solver focuses on vertical sticks and overlooks horizontal modifications to I.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When a horizontal stick is available, consider attaching it to an I to form L, or removing it from L to get I.
